citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research)
description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to evaluate mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering seven mathematical reasoning types and five primary tasks across diverse visual contexts including geometry diagrams, charts, natural images, and scientific figures.
name: MathVista
publisher: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 independent annotations per item for the VQA mathematical reasoning labeling and for the three new datasets; 5 annotations per item for human performance evaluation on testmini
rai:annotatorDemographics: New dataset annotators (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA): graduate students in STEM fields. Human performance evaluators on AMT: required to have a high school diploma or higher (30.9% of problems are high-school level, 10.8% are college-level); required a history of completing more than 5,000 HIT tasks and an acceptance score higher than 0.99. AMT workers for Bard assessment task were compensated at $18 per hour.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement for VQA mathematical reasoning labeling was measured using Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775, indicating substantial consistency. For the three new datasets, inter-annotation consistency rate was 99.2% (only 6 out of 736 newly collected questions exhibited disagreements). For automatic mathematical reasoning category annotation, 94.1% of examples had the exact same set of reasoning types between automatic and human annotations, and 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool (GUI shown in paper figures); Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) for human performance evaluation and Multimodal Bard assessment task
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three expert annotators manually labeled VQA examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using a custom annotation tool with instructions defining mathematical problems. For the three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA), all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. A two-step process was used: (1) each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers; (2) disagreements were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. Mathematical reasoning categories were automatically annotated from source dataset details, then verified by expert annotators who manually labeled 1,000 examples from seven candidates. Human performance was evaluated using Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT), where annotators needed a high school diploma or higher, a history of 5,000+ HIT tasks, and an acceptance score above 0.99; each question was assigned to five annotators with a 20-minute time limit.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is derived from 31 source datasets with heterogeneous origins, which may introduce biases from those sources. Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. The dataset contains 6.57% non-English questions (Chinese and Persian), which may affect model performance on multilingual content. The testmini sampling strategy was designed to maintain distribution similarity to the full test set (KL Divergence = 0.008, TV distance = 0.035). Human performance evaluators were required to have at least a high school diploma, which may not represent all human populations.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from three sources: (1) Nine MathQA datasets in multimodal settings (2,666 examples), including GPS, MWP, and TQA datasets, each limited to up to 400 examples. (2) Nineteen general VQA datasets (2,739 examples) selected from over 70 reviewed datasets that contain math-related instances and are publicly available, filtered using heuristic rules and manual expert annotation. (3) Three newly created datasets — IQTest (228 examples from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms), FunctionQA (400 examples on functional plots), and PaperQA (107 examples from academic paper figures released in August 2023 on HuggingFace).
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of: (1) existing multimodal MathQA datasets (9 datasets) including geometry problem solving, math word problems, and textbook QA; (2) existing general VQA datasets (19 datasets) containing math-related instances; (3) puzzle test figures from online learning platforms (IQTest), functional plot images (FunctionQA), and academic paper figures from papers released in August 2023 on HuggingFace (PaperQA).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023 on HuggingFace. The overall dataset was compiled and released alongside the paper at ICLR 2024.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage may have gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts spanning specific domains (science, college-level math) makes data collection labor-intensive, raising concerns about scalability and generalizability to other domains. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations due to heterogeneous sources; annotations lack unified format and structure. The benchmark was developed at a specific point in time and focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models available then. The answer labels for the test set are not publicly released to prevent data contamination.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning: examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words (e.g., most, least, mean, average, total, sum, percentage, ratio, fraction) were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. Examples were annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, and visual context. The dataset was split into testmini (1,000 examples) and test (5,141 examples) subsets using a sampling strategy to maintain distribution similarity (KL Divergence = 0.008, TV distance = 0.035).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors commit to maintaining the datasets (e.g., refining potential data noise) in response to community feedback, and to evolving the leaderboard in response to new models. An online evaluation platform will be maintained for the test set (whose answer labels are not publicly released to prevent data contamination).
rai:dataSocialImpact: MathVista is intended to drive development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks. Potential applications include solving complex problems in educational disciplines, helping analysts with logical queries about statistical data, and assisting in theorem proving and scientific discovery. The benchmark highlights a significant gap between current AI models and human performance, underscoring the need for improvements in mathematical and visual reasoning capabilities of AI systems.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating mathematical reasoning capabilities of LLMs and LMMs in visual contexts; benchmarking foundation models on tasks requiring fine-grained visual understanding and compositional reasoning; facilitating development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios; assessing AI progress on problems spanning educational disciplines, statistical data analysis, and scientific reasoning; model development validation (testmini subset for those with limited computing resources).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used as an answer extractor to extract short answer text from detailed model responses (achieving >99.5% accuracy on 200 examples). EasyOCR (JaidedAI, 2020) was used to detect OCR text from images for augmented LLM experiments. Multimodal Bard was used to generate image captions for augmented LLM experiments. Heuristic rules using a dictionary of quantity words were used for automatic selection of mathematical problems from VQA datasets.

null_reasons.license: No license terms are discussed in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not explicitly discuss missing data handling such as cloud filtering, missing timestamps, or incomplete records in the dataset collection process.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described; the dataset does not involve filling in missing values.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation such as augmentation, balancing, or resampling is described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper does not discuss collection of personal or sensitive information in the dataset. Images of people appear in some VQA examples but no PII is collected.
